title: AI Lifestyle Product Photos for Your Store | AIVideosUGC
description: Create AI lifestyle product photos that place your item on a kitchen shelf, a desk or a beach towel. Upload one photo, describe the scene and get started.
h1: AI Lifestyle Product Photos in Everyday Settings
lead: AI lifestyle product photos show shoppers where your product belongs. Upload one photo, describe a setting like a sunny patio or a cozy reading nook, and get a square scene built around your item.
secondary_keywords: product in a home setting photo
intro: A plain product shot tells shoppers what your item looks like. A lifestyle photo tells them how it fits into their day: a ceramic mug next to an open book, a backpack hanging on a café chair, a throw blanket draped over a sofa. Scenes like these help people picture owning the product, and they usually take a location, props and a photographer to shoot.

With this tool you upload one clear product photo and describe the setting you want, or pick a ready-made scene. You get a square image with your item placed in that space. It's a good fit for small brands selling home goods, accessories, kitchenware and gifts that need fresh images for product pages, Instagram posts and email banners without booking a shoot every season.

benefits.d: Put your product in a kitchen, a bedroom, a garden or a desk setup so shoppers can imagine it in their own home.
Trade a summer patio for a snowy windowsill without reshooting. Same product, different setting, whenever your store needs a refresh.
Skip the trip for flowers, linens and backdrops. Describe the details you have in mind and the tool builds them into the scene.

steps.d: Use a shot where the item is fully visible and evenly lit. A plain background makes it easier to place in a new scene.
Choose a ready-made scene or write your own, such as "linen bedding, morning light, a small plant on the nightstand."
Save the square image you like. To try a different room or time of day, start a fresh version with a reworded description.

uses.d: Place a lifestyle shot right after your main photo so shoppers see the item in context before they scroll further.
Keep your grid active with styled scenes of products you already sell, no new photoshoot required.
Give newsletters and promo emails an inviting picture that matches the time of year.
Add a styled scene to your handmade listings alongside your close-ups and measurement shots.

faq.q: Can I choose where my product sits in the scene?
faq.a: You can steer it in your description, for example "on the left side of a wooden table." Results won't always follow every word, so short and specific descriptions tend to work well.

faq.q: Will the product look the same as in my original photo?
faq.a: The tool works from your photo to keep the product's shape, color and details. Compare each result with the real item before you publish it, so shoppers get what they see.

faq.q: What lifestyle scenes work well for home goods?
faq.a: Rooms where the item is naturally used: a mug on a breakfast table, a candle on a bathtub ledge, a vase on an entry console. One or two props keep the attention on your product.

faq.q: Can I use lifestyle photos in Facebook or Instagram ads?
faq.a: Yes. Lifestyle scenes work in ads as well as on product pages. Keep words out of the scene itself and add your headline or price later in your ad tool.

overview.h2: Give the product a believable place in the day
overview.d: A lifestyle frame should answer a simple shopper question: where would I use or keep this? Choose a setting that follows the product's real routine, then let one or two supporting props establish context. The item should remain easy to recognize when the scene is viewed at feed size.

overview.h2: Describe the scene like a small shot list
overview.d: Name the surface or room, the time of day, the product position, and one visual accent. “Candle on a stone bath ledge, warm evening light, label facing front” gives the generator more useful direction than “luxury mood.”

input_guide.h2: Prepare a product that can be placed cleanly

items.d: Keep the full item away from the source frame edges so a table, shelf, or bedding scene has room around it.
Point a label, opening, handle, or control toward the camera when that detail helps explain the product.
Photograph bottles upright, bags with their base visible, and decor pieces in the position you want the new scene to echo.
Use a clear, evenly lit product image; the new room can change, but it still starts from what the source shows.
Ask for one room, one surface, one light condition, and no more than a couple of props for a focused composition.

results.h2: A square scene you can plan around

items.d: A lifestyle image uses 24 credits, with the charge visible before you launch it.
The default square shape fits a product-page gallery, a social feed, or an email module.
The setting shows use and placement, while the product remains the subject rather than becoming a generic room photo.
The source and result stay inside your account as you decide where to publish them.
Place the bag on a café chair beside a folded newspaper, with the strap visible and the front panel facing the viewer.
Set the jar on a stone bath ledge beside a rolled towel, with warm evening light and the label kept toward camera.
Show the planter on a bright entry shelf with a few leaves rising above it and clear space around the rim.
Arrange the folded hoodie on a wooden bench beside a beanie, with the chest graphic facing up and no person required.
Place a compact scale beside a mixing bowl on a sunlit counter, keeping the display area visible for inspection later.
Drape the blanket over a neutral sofa arm with a reading lamp in the background, showing the weave at the front fold.

good.d: Items whose value becomes clearer when a room, surface, or daily routine is visible.
Products that benefit from a café, travel, desk, or seasonal setting around them.
A contextual follow-up after the clean product view has already established the item.

not_ideal.t: The only proof of a technical feature
not_ideal.d: Use real specifications and close-ups when a shopper must verify a measurement, port, ingredient, or safety detail.

not_ideal.t: A product that needs strict neutrality
not_ideal.d: Keep the main view plain when marketplace rules or catalog consistency require no props or scene context.

after_download.h2: Turn a scene into a dependable listing asset

items.d: Confirm that the product sits on a believable surface and that the scale does not make it look misleading.
Compare color, shape, label, and count with the real item before publishing the scene.
Place a headline, price, date, or promotion in your editor so the wording stays accurate.

examples.lead: Lifestyle scenes show the product in use, at a believable size, in a setting your buyer recognizes.
